mainTopic: The blood-filled עזרה on ערב פסח, the end of פרק תמיד נשחט, and the start of פרק אלו דברים: which acts of the פסח override שבת
overview: This amud opens by finishing a קשיא against רבי יהודה. He holds that only the life-blood atones, yet his cup of mixed floor blood must contain דם התמצית. The גמרא answers that he holds אין דם מבטל דם, so the valid blood in the cup is not cancelled. A ברייתא then records רבי יהודה asking the חכמים why the עזרה was plugged. They answer that it honored the כהנים to walk in blood. The גמרא solves two problems with this. Wet blood is not a חציצה. As for soiled garments, the walking happened while carrying wood, which is not an עבודה, and during real עבודות the כהנים walked on raised platforms. After two short explanations of the משנה, about the basin of אמורים and carrying the פסח home in its hide, the chapter תמיד נשחט ends. The new chapter's משנה lists which parts of the פסח override שבת. It then presents the dispute over שבות: רבי אליעזר argues by קל וחומר that they override, and רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא bring counter-examples. רבי אליעזר's reply about הזאה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the life-blood atones, so the floor blood is a problem for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the source showing that רבי יהודה holds דם התמצית does not atone. This completes the challenge to his cup-of-mixed-blood practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that comes out with the animal's life atones. Blood that does not come out with the life does not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a source showing that, according to רבי יהודה, only the blood that spurts out at the moment of death atones. The point is to challenge his ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cup filled from the floor surely contains lots of דם התמצית, the blood that drains out after the main spurt. If רבי יהודה holds that this blood does not atone, how can he say that throwing the cup on the מזבח helps? That is the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that oozes or drains out after the initial spurt of שחיטה
The life goes out with it, meaning the main spurt of blood at death
Atones (the blood is valid for זריקה on the מזבח)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a קשיא. These lines are the end of a quoted source, not a brand-new statement. Their job is to show that רבי יהודה excludes דם התמצית.

phrases.english: Blood with which the life goes out — atones.
phrases.notes: The spurt at the moment of שחיטה

phrases.aramaic: דָּם שֶׁאֵין הַנֶּפֶשׁ יוֹצְאָה בּוֹ — אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר.
phrases.english: Blood with which the life does not go out — does not atone.
phrases.notes: This is the leftover blood (דם התמצית) that drains out afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא begun on the previous amud against רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that the cup of mixed floor blood is thrown on the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The floor blood is mostly דם התמצית, which רבי יהודה himself says does not atone, so the cup should be useless

steps.title: Blood does not cancel out blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own principle that אין דם מבטל דם. The valid blood in the cup is not nullified by the larger amount of invalid blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, for he said: blood does not nullify blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יהודה elsewhere holds that one kind of blood cannot cancel out another kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a small amount of something mixed into a larger amount might be בטל, considered gone. רבי יהודה holds that when blood mixes with blood, there is no ביטול. So even a little valid blood in the cup still counts and can atone.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere
Blood does not nullify blood
Nullification of a minority mixed into a majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns a contradiction into consistency. רבי יהודה's practice works precisely because of another known view of his.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
for he said: blood does not nullify blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the speaker's consistent view elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The invalid דם התמצית in the cup would outweigh and cancel the valid blood
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, blood is never nullified by blood, so the valid blood in the cup still atones

steps.title: Why plug the courtyard drains according to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה challenging the חכמים. If they do not use the floor blood, why was the עזרה plugged on ערב פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said to the חכמים, according to your words, why do they plug up the courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה attacks the opposing view. He uses the known practice of plugging the drains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה argues that the drains of the עזרה were plugged so the blood would collect on the floor. In his view, the purpose was to fill the cup. If the חכמים say no cup was filled, the plugging seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or view
They plug or stop up (the drains)
The Temple courtyard

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said to the Sages:
According to your words, why do they plug the courtyard?
phrases.notes: He means the courtyard's drainage outlets.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לַחֲכָמִים: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי יהודה to his own attack on the חכמים
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that no cup of floor blood was collected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The established practice of plugging the drains only makes sense if the floor blood was needed

steps.title: It honors the כהנים to walk in blood
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the plugging had a different purpose. It was a praise for the כהנים to walk deep in קרבן blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: it is a praise for the sons of אהרן that they walk up to their ankles in blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give another reason for plugging the drains, unrelated to collecting blood. It showed the כהנים' love and devotion to the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים accept the practice but reinterpret its purpose. The pooled blood showed the huge number of קרבנות and the כהנים' eagerness. So the practice does not prove רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Praise or honor
The sons of אהרן, i.e., the כהנים
Their ankles (literally knees or lower-leg joints)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שֶׁבַח הוּא לִבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: They said to him: it is a praise for the sons of Aaron
that they walk up to their ankles in blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שֶׁבַח הוּא לִבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the purpose of the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plugging the drains was done to collect blood for a cup
steps.terutzMaskana: Plugging was done to honor the כהנים, who walked in the pooled blood

steps.title: The blood should create a barrier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים's answer. Blood under the כהנים' feet should be a חציצה between them and the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't it interpose?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4. A כהן must stand directly on the floor of the עזרה, and the blood seems to block that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that nothing may separate the כהן's feet from the floor during עבודה. Walking in a layer of blood seems to create exactly such a barrier. That would invalidate the עבודה, so it can hardly be called a praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Interposes or forms a barrier (from חציצה)
A barrier between body and floor (or water, in טבילה) that invalidates

phrases.english: But doesn't it interpose?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that it was praiseworthy for the כהנים to walk in blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood under the feet would be a חציצה and invalidate the כהנים' עבודה

steps.title: Wet blood is not a barrier
steps.stepSummary: Because the blood is moist, it does not count as a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is moist, and it does not interpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wet blood does not separate. Only dry blood would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חציצה must be something that sticks and forms a distinct layer. Fresh, liquid blood does not count that way. So the כהנים' feet are still considered touching the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist or wet
Forms a barrier

phrases.english: It is moist, and it does not interpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in the state of the substance (wet vs. dry)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any blood under the feet is a חציצה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only dry blood is a חציצה; wet blood is not

steps.title: A ברייתא proves wet substances do not interpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that blood, ink, milk, and honey interpose when dry but not when wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: blood, ink, milk, and honey, when dry, interpose. When moist, they do not interpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from step 6 with a ברייתא that states this exact rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists sticky liquids and draws the line at dryness. Blood is explicitly on the list. This confirms that the wet blood in the עזרה is not a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
Ink
Dry

phrases.english: As it was taught: blood, ink, milk, and honey,
when dry — they interpose;
when moist — they do not interpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 6
steps.raayaObject: Wet blood is not a חציצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: blood, ink, milk, and honey interpose only when dry

steps.title: The priestly garments would get soiled
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: walking in blood would stain the בגדי כהונה, and soiled garments invalidate the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But their garments get soiled! And we learned: if his garments were soiled and he performed the service, his service is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the חכמים's answer. A משנה rules that עבודה done in dirty garments is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the blood is not a חציצה, the כהנים' long garments would drag in the blood and become stained. The בגדי כהונה must be clean and dignified. So walking in blood should ruin their עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Become soiled or dirtied
Their garments (literally their vessels or clothes)
Soiled or stained
His service is invalid

phrases.english: But don't their garments become soiled?
And we learned: if his garments were soiled and he performed the service —
his service is invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent challenge to the חכמים's answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that it was praiseworthy for the כהנים to walk in blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their garments would become stained, and a משנה rules that עבודה in soiled garments is invalid

steps.title: They cannot lift their garments, because these must fit exactly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the כהנים raised their garments. It immediately rejects this, since the garments must be exactly the כהן's size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they raised their garments, but it was taught: 'מדו בד' means his garment must be according to his measure, not too short and not too long!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a possible way out of the challenge: lifting the garments to keep them clean. Then it shoots that idea down with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מדו בד' is read as requiring the garment to match the כהן's measure exactly. Hiking up the garment makes it effectively too short. So the כהנים could not have raised their garments, and the problem of soiling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a proposed answer)
They raise or lift up
His linen garment (ויקרא ו:ג), expounded as 'his measure'
According to his size or measure

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase וכי תימא introduces an answer only to reject it. Do not mistake 'they raised their garments' for the גמרא's conclusion.

phrases.english: And if you say that they raised their garments,
but wasn't it taught: 'his linen garment [middo]' — his garment according to his measure,
phrases.notes: There's a play on words here: מדו sounds like מדתו.

phrases.english: that it be neither too short nor too long!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects a possible answer to step 8, strengthening the קשיא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggested answer that the כהנים lifted their garments
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Lifted garments no longer match the כהן's measure, which the פסוק 'מדו בד' requires

steps.title: They walked in blood while carrying limbs, which is not a true עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The walking in blood happened while carrying limbs to the כבש of the מזבח. That is not a formal עבודה, so soiled garments do not invalidate anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the carrying of the limbs to the ramp, which is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the soiled-garments problem. The כהנים walked in the blood during a task it claims is not an עבודה. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that soiled garments invalidate applies only to an actual עבודה. This answer claims that carrying the limbs to the כבש is only preparation, so stained garments would cause no פסול. Step 11 will challenge whether this carrying is truly not an עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the sacrificial limbs
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
It is not a formal Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: The plugged עזרה is explained by the חכמים as an honor for the כהנים. Two problems were raised. חציצה: wet blood does not interpose. Soiled garments: this step suggests the walking happened while carrying limbs to the כבש, but step 11 rejects that, and step 12 gives the final answer (carrying wood to the מערכה). Meanwhile, רבי יהודה's cup works because אין דם מבטל דם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer introduces the distinction between preparatory tasks and formal עבודות. Step 11 shows that carrying limbs falls on the עבודה side of that line.

phrases.english: During the carrying of the limbs to the ramp —
which is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 8 after the rejected answer in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a non-עבודה activity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהנים walked in blood while doing actual עבודה, so soiled garments would invalidate it
steps.terutzMaskana: They walked in blood only while carrying limbs to the כבש, which is not a formal עבודה, so soiling causes no פסול

steps.title: Carrying limbs to the ramp is a real Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 10. Carrying the אברים to the כבש requires כהונה, and a ברייתא learns it from a פסוק, so it counts as an עבודה after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not a rite? But since it requires priesthood, it is a rite! As it was taught: 'And the כהן shall bring it all to the altar.' This refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10. That answer said carrying limbs to the כבש is not an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 needed this task to be a non-עבודה, so that soiled garments would not matter. The גמרא proves the opposite. The פסוק says 'the כהן shall bring it,' so only a כהן may carry the limbs. A task that only a כהן may do is a real עבודה, which means soiled garments would invalidate it.

keyTerms.meaning: Priesthood: a task that only a כהן may do
Carrying (bringing something to its place in the service)
The limbs of the קרבן
But behold! (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'carrying.' Here the limbs are carried to the כבש, and that is a real עבודה. In the next step, wood is carried to the מערכה, and that is not.

phrases.english: And it is not [a rite]?
phrases.notes: This pushes back on what was said in Step 10.

phrases.english: But since it requires priesthood
it is a rite!
As it was taught: 'And the priest shall bring it all to the altar,'
this is the carrying of limbs to the ramp!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's claim that carrying limbs to the כבש is not an עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A task that requires כהונה is an עבודה, and a ברייתא learns from a פסוק that a כהן must carry the limbs to the כבש.

steps.title: The walking in blood happened while carrying wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its answer. The כהנים walked in the blood while carrying wood to the מערכה, and that is not an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was while carrying wood to the wood pile, which is not a rite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the answer from Step 10 and gives a new one. The walking in blood happened during a task that is not an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying wood to the fire-pile on the מזבח is not counted as an עבודה. So even if a כהן's garments got soiled while doing it, nothing is invalidated. This answers the challenge from Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected answer)
Wood
The wood pile (fire) on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather: while carrying wood to the wood pile,
which is not a rite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that Step 11 rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the case (which activity involved walking in blood)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The walking in blood happened while carrying limbs to the כבש
steps.terutzMaskana: The walking in blood happened while carrying wood to the מערכה, which is not an עבודה, so soiled garments do not matter

steps.title: How did they walk during real services?
steps.stepSummary: If the floor was full of blood, how did the כהנים walk while carrying limbs or blood, which are real עבודות?
steps.simpleTranslation: When carrying limbs to the ramp and carrying blood, how did they walk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Step 12 covered carrying wood, but some carrying is a real עבודה. How did the כהנים avoid soiling their garments then?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 only solved the problem for carrying wood. Carrying limbs and carrying blood are real עבודות, and soiled garments would invalidate them. So the גמרא needs to know how the כהנים walked across the bloody floor during those tasks.

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate / however
How?
They walked / would go

phrases.english: While carrying limbs to the ramp
and while carrying blood,
at any rate, how did they walk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out what Step 12's answer did not cover
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the כהנים walked without soiling their garments during carrying that is a real עבודה

steps.title: They walked on raised platforms
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים walked on raised platforms above the floor, so their garments stayed clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would walk on platforms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13. During real עבודות, the כהנים walked on raised platforms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking on raised platforms kept the כהנים out of the blood on the floor. Their garments stayed clean, so these עבודות were valid.

keyTerms.meaning: They walk
Platform / raised bench
Short for עַל, meaning 'on'

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways the garments stayed valid: carrying wood is not an עבודה, so soiling does not matter; and for real עבודות, the כהנים walked on raised platforms.

phrases.english: That they would walk on platforms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They walked on raised platforms and so avoided the blood on the floor

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on preparing the sacrificial parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the animal was hung and skinned, cut open, and its אמורים were put into a basin 'to burn them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How does one hang and skin it' and so on. He tore it open and they removed its sacrificial parts. He put them in a basin to burn them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question on one word in that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the base text for the next step. The phrase 'to burn them' sounds like the same person who put the parts in the basin would also burn them. The next step questions exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: Hang (the animal)
Skin / flay
The sacrificial parts burned on the מזבח
A large basin
To burn (offer up) on the מזבח

phrases.english: How does one suspend and flay, etc.
He tore it open, and they removed its sacrificial parts.
He placed them in a basin to burn them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic by quoting the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After skinning, the animal was opened, its אמורים were removed, and they were placed in a basin to be burned

steps.title: Did that same person burn them himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does 'to burn them' mean that this same person himself burned the parts?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that he himself would burn them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. It sounds as if the person who put the parts in the basin also burned them, which does not seem right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'to burn them' links the burning to the person who put the parts in the basin. Nothing says he had to be the one to burn them on the מזבח. So the wording seems inaccurate.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a doubtful reading)
He himself
Burns (offers up)

phrases.english: Is that to say that he himself
would burn them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הוּא גּוּפֵיהּ הֲוָה מַקְטַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה quoted in Step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording suggests the same person must do the burning, and that is not required

steps.title: Reading it as 'to be burned on the altar'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the phrase as 'to burn them on the מזבח.' The basin was a step toward burning, not a statement about who would burn them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'in order to burn them on the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 16 by rereading the משנה. The phrase tells us where the parts were going, not who would burn them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added words 'on the מזבח,' the phrase describes the purpose of the basin. The parts were collected so they could later be burned on the מזבח, by whichever כהן did that job.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it as (corrects or reinterprets a text)
On top of
The altar

phrases.english: Say:
in order to burn them on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person who put the parts in the basin must burn them himself
steps.terutzMaskana: The parts were put in the basin to be burned on the מזבח by whoever does that job

steps.title: How each person carried his Paschal lamb home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the first group leaving, then cites a ברייתא: each person put his פסח in its hide and slung it over his shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The first group went out' and so on. It was taught: each and every one puts his Paschal lamb in its hide and slings it behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and adds a ברייתא describing how people carried their פסח out of the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the groups left. The ברייתא adds the detail: the meat stayed wrapped in its own hide, and the owner carried it slung over his shoulder behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: A group (one of the three shifts that offered the פסח)
Hide / skin
Slings (over the shoulder)

phrases.english: The first group went out, etc.
It was taught: each and every one
places his Paschal lamb in its hide,
and slings it behind him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person carried his פסח home in its hide, slung over his shoulder

steps.title: Like Arab merchants
steps.stepSummary: רב עיליש compares this way of carrying to the way Arab merchants carry their goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עיליש said: like Arab merchants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עיליש gives a picture to explain the ברייתא. The people carried their פסח the way Arab traders carry their loads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new law. It helps us picture the scene: the load was slung over the shoulder and hung behind the carrier, as traveling Arab merchants carried their goods.

keyTerms.meaning: In the manner of Arab merchants

steps.whatToRemember: The פסח was carried home wrapped in its hide and slung over the shoulder, like Arab merchants carry their goods.

phrases.english: Rav Ilish said:
In the manner of Arab merchants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא in Step 18 with a picture
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slinging the פסח behind oneself is the way Arab merchants carry their goods

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter תמיד נשחט
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing line of the fifth chapter of פסחים, פרק תמיד נשחט.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'תמיד נשחט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the chapter תמיד נשחט with the traditional closing formula. Nothing new is being argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each chapter of the תלמוד ends with הדרן, a promise to come back and learn it again. The chapter is named for its first words, which describe when the daily תמיד offering was slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula for closing a chapter
'The תמיד is slaughtered': the name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The Tamid is slaughtered'
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose last discussion was the carrying of the פסח home in its hide.

steps.title: The parts of the פסח service that override שבת, and the parts that do not
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists four parts of the פסח service that override שבת and two that do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: These things in the פסח override שבת: slaughtering it, sprinkling its blood, cleaning out its innards, and burning its fats on the מזבח. But roasting it and washing its innards do not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It tells us which parts of preparing the קרבן פסח may be done on שבת when ערב פסח falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parts that override שבת are core Temple services that must be done during the day of the fourteenth. Roasting and washing the innards can wait until after nightfall, when שבת is over. So they do not push aside שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Override (push aside) שבת: permitted even though it is normally forbidden on שבת
Sprinkling (throwing) its blood on the מזבח
Cleaning out its innards (squeezing out the waste)
Burning its fats on the מזבח
Roasting (the פסח is eaten roasted)
Rinsing (washing) its innards

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מיחוי (cleaning out the innards, which overrides שבת) with הדחה (washing the innards, which does not). They sound alike but get opposite rulings.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are the matters in the Paschal offering
phrases.notes: Opening words of the new chapter, which gives the chapter its name

phrases.english: that override Shabbat:
its slaughter, and the sprinkling of its blood,
and cleaning out its innards, and burning its fats.
phrases.notes: These must be done during the day

phrases.english: But its roasting and the washing of its innards
do not override Shabbat.
phrases.notes: They can wait until after שבת

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים בַּפֶּסַח דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter, sprinkling the blood, cleaning the innards, and burning the fats override שבת. Roasting and washing the innards do not.

steps.title: Carrying, bringing from outside the תחום, and cutting a wart: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that three preparatory acts do not override שבת. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Carrying it, bringing it from outside the תחום, and cutting off its wart do not override שבת. רבי אליעזר says: they do override.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three more acts that the first opinion says may not be done on שבת. Then רבי אליעזר argues that they are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three acts could have been done before שבת, and each one is forbidden on שבת only מדרבנן (a שבות). The question is whether a rabbinic prohibition gives way for the פסח. The first opinion says no. רבי אליעזר says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying it (lit. 'mounting it' on one's shoulders)
תחום שבת: the boundary beyond which one may not walk on שבת
Its wart, a blemish that disqualifies the animal

phrases.english: Carrying it, and bringing it from outside the Shabbat boundary,
and cutting off its wart
do not override Shabbat.
Rabbi Eliezer says: they override.
phrases.notes: The dispute that drives the rest of this passage

steps.triggerLanguage: הַרְכָּבָתוֹ, וַהֲבָאָתוֹ מִחוּץ לַתְּחוּם, וַחֲתִיכַת יַבַּלְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list and adds a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, carrying, bringing from outside the תחום, and cutting a wart do not override שבת. According to רבי אליעזר, they do.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues: if slaughter, a full מלאכה, overrides שבת, then these acts, which are only a שבות, should surely override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: Isn't it logical? If slaughter, which is forbidden as a מלאכה, overrides שבת, then shouldn't these acts, which are forbidden only as a שבות, override שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a reason for his opinion. He uses a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלאכה is a Torah-level prohibition, and a שבות is a lighter rabbinic one. The Torah already lets the פסח push aside the heavier prohibition. So logic says it should push aside the lighter one too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it logical?': opens a קל וחומר
A Torah-forbidden act of work on שבת
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וַהֲלֹא דִּין הוּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: Is it not logical?

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: If slaughter, which is forbidden as a labor,
overrides Shabbat,
these, which are forbidden only by rabbinic decree,
should they not override Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אליעזר's opinion from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That carrying, bringing from outside the תחום, and cutting the wart override שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר: slaughter, a מלאכה, overrides שבת, so a lighter שבות should too.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: יום טוב breaks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע points to יום טוב, where מלאכה for food is permitted but שבות remains forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: יום טוב proves otherwise. On it they permitted acts forbidden as a מלאכה, yet acts forbidden as a שבות remain forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's logic. He shows a case where a heavier prohibition is permitted but a lighter one is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב one may cook and slaughter for food, even though these are Torah-level מלאכות. Still, rabbinic prohibitions stay in force. So permitting a מלאכה does not automatically mean a שבות is permitted, and the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove': introduces a counter-example that breaks a קל וחומר
A Festival day, when cooking and similar work for food is allowed

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: יוֹם טוֹב יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: a Festival will prove otherwise,
for they permitted on it things forbidden as labor,
yet things forbidden by rabbinic decree are prohibited on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logic of the קל וחומר, not רבי אליעזר's facts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Permitting a מלאכה does not always mean a שבות is permitted, as יום טוב shows.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: optional acts cannot teach about a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects רבי יהושע's proof, because the work allowed on יום טוב is optional, while the פסח is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: What is this, יהושע?! What proof can you bring from something optional to a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר pushes back on רבי יהושע's counter-example. He says it is not a fair comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is רשות, meaning a person does not have to do it. It makes sense that rabbinic limits stay in place for optional acts. That does not show they stay in place when a מצוה like the פסח is at stake, so the קל וחומר still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Optional: permitted but not required
A commanded religious obligation

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מָה זֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ?!
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: What is this, Yehoshua?!
phrases.notes: A sharp expression of surprise at a weak proof

phrases.english: What proof is there from the optional to a מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהושע's counter-example from step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יום טוב work is optional (רשות), but the פסח is a מצוה, so the cases are not comparable.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: הזאה is a מצוה and a שבות, yet it does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא brings a counter-example that is a מצוה: sprinkling the purifying water. It is only a שבות, yet it does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא answered and said: הזאה (sprinkling) will prove it. It is for a מצוה and it is only a שבות, yet it does not override שבת. So you too should not be surprised about these acts. Even though they are for a מצוה and are only a שבות, they do not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא steps in to defend רבי יהושע's side. He brings a new counter-example that fixes the weakness רבי אליעזר pointed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling פרה אדומה water on a person who is טמא מת lets him bring the פסח, so it serves a מצוה. It is forbidden on שבת only מדרבנן, yet it is not done on שבת. That shows a שבות can stay in force even for a מצוה, which breaks רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling פרה אדומה water to purify someone who is טמא מת
Responded
Do not be surprised

steps.whatToRemember: The debate is about whether a שבות gives way for the פסח. רבי אליעזר says yes, by a קל וחומר from slaughter. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא say no. רבי עקיבא's proof avoids the רשות/מצוה objection, because הזאה is both a מצוה and a שבות. The next step shows that רבי אליעזר disputes even this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי אליעזר's next reply, in which he claims that הזאה itself should override שבת by the same קל וחומר. The whole argument turns on whether rabbinic prohibitions give way for a time-bound מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva responded and said:
Sprinkling will prove it, for it is for the sake of a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, וְאֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and it is only a rabbinic prohibition, yet it does not override Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: So you too, do not be surprised about these,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן מִשּׁוּם מִצְוָה, וְהֵן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת,
phrases.english: that even though they are for a מצוה and they are only a rabbinic prohibition,
they do not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְאָמַר: הַזָּאָה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's objection in step 25 with a counter-example that involves a מצוה, and so renews the attack on the קל וחומר of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from step 23.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A שבות can remain forbidden even for a מצוה, as הזאה shows. So permitting a מלאכה for the פסח does not prove that a שבות is permitted.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר extends his logic to sprinkling too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects רבי עקיבא's counter-example. He says his קל וחומר also applies to הזאה, so הזאה should also override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I apply my reasoning to that case too. If שחיטה, which is forbidden as a full מלאכה, overrides שבת, then surely הזאה, which is forbidden only as a שבות, should override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי עקיבא's counter-example. He refuses to treat הזאה as proof against him and runs his same argument on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא assumed that everyone agrees הזאה does not override שבת. רבי אליעזר attacks that assumption, not his own argument. He says the same קל וחומר shows that הזאה also overrides שבת, so the counter-example falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the purifying water (made with ashes of the פרה אדומה) on a person who is טמא מת
'And regarding it I also reason': I apply my argument to your example too
Forbidden only as a rabbinic rest restriction, not as a full Torah labor
'Is it not logical?': the closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר accepts that הזאה is forbidden on שבת and then searches for a distinction. He does the reverse: he argues that הזאה is also permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי עקיבא's next reply. Now the argument is about whether הזאה itself overrides שבת, not only about the original three acts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him (to Rabbi Akiva):
And regarding it (sprinkling) I also apply my reasoning:
phrases.notes: He will not accept sprinkling as an agreed-upon counter-example.

phrases.english: If slaughter,
which is forbidden as a full Torah labor,
overrides Shabbat,
then sprinkling, which is forbidden only as a rabbinic restriction,
is it not logical that it overrides Shabbat?
phrases.notes: This is the same 'lighter to heavier' reasoning as in step 23, now used for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְעָלֶיהָ אֲנִי דָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's counter-example from step 26 by applying the step 23 קל וחומר to הזאה itself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא's counter-example by denying its premise that הזאה does not override שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא assumed a ruling about הזאה that רבי אליעזר does not accept. By the same קל וחומר, הזאה also overrides שבת.
